headline: Testimony continues on Kīhei and West Maui plan changes

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: The committee heard public testimony on two resolutions to amend the Kīhei-Mākena and West Maui Community Plans, then took a break.
meeting.recap: The only agenda item, heard for the third time, was Resolutions 26-129 and 26-130.[[0:15:57]] An owner at a Kīhei oceanfront condo asked that her building get the same hotel-rezoning consideration as similar properties.[[0:20:36]] She said flood insurance, when offered, costs about $10,000 per unit each year.[[0:22:31]] A journalist asked why the County would create carve-outs from Bill 9 that could reduce its benefits.[[0:30:53]] A Maui Housing Hui researcher said the burden of housing costs on Maui residents has not improved in several years.[[0:34:37]] A speaker for the Maui Tomorrow Foundation said the group opposes the resolutions.[[0:46:20]] A Sierra Club Maui Group speaker said this process is not one size fits all.[[0:58:42]] Another testifier urged the council not to advance the plan amendments and rezoning in isolation.[[1:20:35]] She pointed to SB 3034, a state bill from last term to start a buyback program.[[1:29:17]] Another testifier asked members to vote no.[[1:37:15]]

moments.q: A journalist sums up his two questions about Bill 9

trackerIssues.title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties

issues.oneLine: A council member said one property in Resolution 26-130 is on the shoreline and was completely burnt down.
issues.brief: The council member said the burnt-down property could be rebuilt as housing or as a short-term rental if it got hotel zoning.[[#1]]
